Winter chain care: keep your drivetrain running through the salt season

26

By Jonas Albrecht · 18 November 2025 · Print version

27 28

Every January we replace more chains than in the rest of the year together. Road salt and wet grit turn a chain into sandpaper, and a worn chain then wears out the cassette and chainrings as well. Ten minutes a week keeps most of that away.

29 30

Clean it, do not drown it

31 32

Wipe the chain with a dry rag while you turn the cranks backwards. If it is very dirty, use a little degreaser on the rag, not a jet of water: a pressure washer pushes water past the seals into the bearings.

33 34

Use a wet lube or wax, and wipe off the extra

35 36

In winter a wet lube lasts longer between rain rides. Put one drop on each roller, turn the cranks for a minute, and then wipe the outside of the chain. Lube that stays on the outside only collects dirt.

37 38

Measure wear once a month

39

A chain checker costs a few euros. When it shows 0.5 % wear on an 11- or 12-speed chain, or 0.75 % on a chain with fewer gears, change the chain before it damages the cassette.

40 41

If you would rather leave it to us, the chain is checked and cleaned in every service – see our repair prices.

How to choose tyre pressure for city riding

26

By Lea Hartmann · 3 March 2026

27 28

The number printed on the tyre sidewall is a maximum, not a recommendation. On cobbles and patched asphalt, most riders are faster and more comfortable a good way below it.

29 30

Start from the tyre width

31 32

As a starting point for a rider of about 75 kg: 28 mm tyres at 5 to 5.5 bar, 35 mm tyres at 3.5 to 4 bar, and 47 mm tyres at 2.5 to 3 bar. Put about 0.3 bar less in the front than in the rear.

33 34

Then adjust by feel

35

If the bike bounces over cobbles, let some air out. If the tyre squirms in corners or you feel the rim hit an edge, add some. Check the pressure every two weeks: tyres lose air slowly even without a puncture.

36

content.text:
CSS is clean, nothing hidden there. I've got the full picture now. Here's what's actually keeping this site out of Google:

**Blocking indexing outright**
1. `robots.txt` disallows `/blog/` entirely — the whole blog is invisible to Google, in both languages.
2. `services.html` — the pricing page linked right off the homepage — has `noindex, nofollow`. Your best commercial page is hidden, and `nofollow` also stops link credit from reaching the contact page.
3. The "Shop" nav link on **every page** is `<span onclick="location.href='/shop/'">` instead of a real `<a href="/shop/">`. No `href` means Google has no reliable link to follow — the whole shop section is starved of internal links.

**Broken links / sitemap errors**
4. Both blog posts and the shop page link to `/repairs.html`, which doesn't exist — should be `/services.html`. That's a dead-end for crawlers and visitors.
5. `sitemap.xml` lists that same broken `/repairs.html` (not `/services.html`), and also lists `/thanks.html`, a noindex confirmation page that shouldn't be submitted at all.

**Broken German/English signals (hreflang)**
6. `contact.html` and `de/kontakt.html` both use `hreflang="ge"` — not a valid language code (German is `de`). Google ignores malformed hreflang, so it isn't linking your EN/DE contact pages as translations.
7. `de/leistungen.html` has no hreflang pointing back to the English services page, so once we un-block it, the pairing needs to be reciprocal.

**Smaller but real**
8. `blog/tyre-pressure.html` canonical URL uses `http://` instead of `https://`.
9. `shop/tubeless-kit.html` has two conflicting `<link rel="canonical">` tags — one wrongly points at `/shop/`.
10. All three blog pages share the identical generic title/description ("Blog | Werkbank Cycles") instead of per-article ones — this hurts how each article ranks and shows up in results.
11. No local-business structured data (JSON-LD), which is one of the strongest levers for a bike shop to show up in Google's local/maps results for "bike repair Berlin."

I'll fix all of these directly in the code now.

This is well-formed JSON-LD. All fixes are in place. Summary of what changed:

**Fixed (all directly in the code):**
1. `robots.txt` — removed `Disallow: /blog/`, so the blog can be crawled and indexed in both languages.
2. `services.html` — removed `noindex, nofollow`; your prices page can now be indexed and pass link value.
3. All 12 pages — replaced the JS-only `<span onclick>` "Shop" link with a real `<a href="/shop/">`, so crawlers can discover and follow it (also dropped the now-unused `.nav-link` CSS rule).
4. `blog/winter-chain-care.html` and `shop/tubeless-kit.html` — fixed dead links to `/repairs.html` → `/services.html`.
5. `sitemap.xml` — fixed that same broken URL and removed `/thanks.html` (a noindex confirmation page that shouldn't be submitted).
6. `contact.html` and `de/kontakt.html` — fixed `hreflang="ge"` (invalid) → `"de"`, and added missing `x-default` tags.
7. `de/leistungen.html` — added the missing reciprocal `hreflang="en"`/`x-default` back to `services.html`.
8. `blog/tyre-pressure.html` — canonical URL fixed from `http://` to `https://`.
9. `shop/tubeless-kit.html` — removed a duplicate, conflicting canonical tag that pointed at the shop index instead of itself.
10. Both blog articles — replaced the identical generic "Blog | Werkbank Cycles" title/description with unique, content-specific ones.
11. `blog/winter-chain-care-print.html` — added `noindex` (near-duplicate of the main article, consistent with how `thanks.html` is already handled).
12. Added `BicycleStore` JSON-LD structured data (name, address, phone, hours) to both homepages — helps Google's local pack/maps results for "bike repair Berlin," using only facts already published on the page.

**Worth knowing but not something I changed:**
- The blog only exists in English (`de/kontakt.html` even labels it "Blog (Englisch)"). That's a content decision, not a bug — if ranking in German search matters, translating or writing German posts would help, but that's new content the shop should approve, not something to fabricate.
- Consider adding a free Google Business Profile listing tied to the same address/phone/hours — that's usually the single biggest lever for local "bike shop near me" visibility, but it's an account action outside this codebase.

Once these are live, use Google Search Console for both properties to request re-indexing of `/services.html` and the `/blog/` pages so Google picks up the changes faster.
